title: Three Ways Vinicius Jr Can Turn Around His Real Madrid Form
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath8:00 PM EDTVinícius Jr is threatening to become a problem player. /  Maciej Rogowski/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesIt’s been a tough few months for Vinícius Jr.
The Brazilian has openly admitted that Brazil’s disappointing round of 16 exit to Norway at the World Cup was hard to take and had a knock-on effect on his confidence.

By the first international break, Vinícius Jr had scored just once for Real Madrid in the 2026–27 season—a stat which has loomed especially large given the mega-money contract extension the forward recently signed after over a year of protracted negotiations and flirtations with Arsenal.
While Madrid manager José Mourinho has defended Vinícius from the Bernabéu boo boys, he has admitted the superstar, who came second in the 2024 Ballon d’Or vote, “isn’t at his best.”

The Madrid derby defeat was a low point for both Los Blancos and Vinícius personally, with the forward putting in a limp display before being substituted after less than an hour.

A break from the Madrid fishbowl for Brazil duty has largely failed to provide the reset the 26-year-old needs, with his showing in the friendly win over India in Kolkata raising eyebrows. Vinícius completed only seven of 13 passes, attempted zero dribbles and missed one big chance against the team ranked 138th in the world by FIFA before coming off at halftime.

The star’s only goal in three matches this international break has come from the penalty spot—the fourth in a 4–2 win over Australia—and he looks far from the world-beating match-winner of recent memory.
Incredibly, a player who has scored 129 goals—including two in Champions League finals—is threatening to become a problem for Real Madrid.

The Vinícius Jr situation is already one of the dominant narratives of Madrid’s season, with the club trailing Barcelona by six points in La Liga and in danger of a third straight season without a major trophy.
Madrid have a crunch period coming up with the first Clásico of the season rearing into view on Oct. 25, and will need all their stars firing to compete on all fronts this season.

Dealing with an out-of-sorts superstar like Vinícius is one of the first big tests for Mourinho upon his return. Does the 63-year-old, once hailed for his man-management skills, still have what to takes to get the best out of his players?

Mbappé and Vinícius Jr have struggled to connect. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesOne of the big issues for Madrid ever since the arrival of Kylian Mbappé is the space he and Vinícius occupy on the pitch.
L’Equipe posted a damning graphic after the Madrid derby that showed the average positions of all Madrid players, with Mbappé and Vinícius essentially on top of one another.
The central problem is that Mbappé is a striker who drifts to the left rather than staying central, inevitably meaning the two players often overlap—and not in a good way.

Mourinho has made Mbappé key to his plans as the spearhead of the 4-2-3-1 system and it has paid dividends, with the Frenchman scoring seven in seven in La Liga so far in 2026–27. However, it has, in part, curbed the effectiveness of Vinícius.
No manager has pulled it off it yet, but some systemic tinkering might allow both to flourish without cramping each other’s styles. What that would actually look like though is hard to say.

Vinícius Jr hasn’t felt the love from Madrid fans recently. / Richard Haines/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesVinícius has always been a streaky player rather than a consistent goal threat and has thrived when made to feel like the main man.

Prior to Mbappé’s arrival, he shone as the star in the Champions League-winning team of 2023–24 when he was relied upon to produce those moments of magic and then felt the love of the Bernabéu when he did.

The contract saga has seemingly damaged the Brazilian’s standing among the notoriously demanding Madrid supporters, who have booed and whistled him regularly this season as penance for daring to a) drag out his renewal talks and b) be out of form.
